Lessons.Title: More Questions about Scaled Bar Graphs
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Illustrative Mathematics K–5, Grade 3 Unit 1 Lesson 8. Standard 3.MD.B.3. Learning goal: solve ONE- and TWO-STEP more-than/fewer-than problems from scaled bar graphs within 100, using addition/subtraction and the source MLR6 Three Reads problem-solving routine. This is a SOURCE-ALIGNED lesson, not a generic one-step bar drill. Warm-up 10 minutes, New School Year Activity 1 20 minutes, Trees Activity 2 15 minutes, lesson synthesis 10 minutes, original Cool-down 5 minutes; teacher-led optional centers and a Student Section Summary.

Warm-up — Number Talk: Repeated Addition (10 minutes). Source gives FOUR expressions in EXACT order: five copies of two (2+2+2+2+2=10), six copies of two (=12), six copies of five (=30), seven copies of five (=35). Teacher asks students to use the prior number talk to see one MORE equal addend in the next expression, privately think one minute then discuss multiple methods, including skip-counting or adding one extra 2 or 5. The source task is mathematical reasoning, not a silent auto-pass of one product.

Activity 1 — New School Year (20 minutes). Source graph Feelings About the New School Year uses original heights Excited 55, Nervous 23 and Curious 25 with vertical axis 0–60 by 5s. Source learner question asks how many MORE are excited than those who are nervous OR curious: combine 23+25=48; subtract from 55 giving 7. Alternative valid TWO-STEP method: 55−23=32, then 32−25=7; or 55−25−23=7. Teacher introduces MLR6 THREE READS with a deliberately unrevealed problem during first graph-only view: First read focuses on situation, second on measurable quantities, third reveals the precise question and mathematical strategies. Student responses record all three reasoning stages for teacher review; human partners and chart viewing are teacher-led.

Activity 2 — Use Bar Graphs to Solve Problems (15 minutes). Source graph Trees I Saw on the Way Home, with a vertical axis 0–100 in 10s, contains Oak 29, Pine 82, Maple 15, Fir 58. Four original Student Facing problems are: Pine more than Fir =24; Pine more than Oak or Maple combined =82−(29+15)=38; Oak fewer than Pine =53; Oak or Maple fewer than Fir =58−(29+15)=14. Learners may solve by first adding both compared categories or subtracting sequentially, then compare two valid mathematical methods, including tens-and-ones. Group discussion and MLR8 rehearsal remain teacher-reviewed. Source bar heights 29,82,15,58 fall BETWEEN ticks and are displayed accurately with independent first-party graphics.

Lesson synthesis (10 minutes) BEFORE Cool-down: teacher displays pupil equations, compares strategies including counting by tens, subtracting tens then ones and solving a two-step compare using Three Reads independently. Student Section Summary consolidates scaled picture graphs and bar graphs and questions using more/fewer language. The first-edition SOURCE Cool-down 'Reading Time' (5 minutes) shows approximate Favorite Time to Read bars: Morning ABOUT 11–12, Lunchtime 25, Afternoon 23, Evenings 44, with a 0–50 axis by FIVES. Two original questions: how many FEWER Morning than Afternoon (teacher guide exemplar about 12) and how many MORE Evening than Morning OR Lunchtime combined (guide exemplar 7). The source teacher guide's two sample calculations read slightly different plausible Morning values (11 and 12), so results are APPROXIMATE and must be judged by a human teacher; NEVER fixed-passed by the numeric helper. Pupils write two distinct equations. Separate fictional Edulytics Adventure/Science/Comics drills remain optional EXTRA, not the publisher source Cool-down.

KeyConcepts.Title: Three Reads problem-solving routine
KeyConcepts.Definition: Read the same mathematical situation for a different purpose on each pass.
KeyConcepts.Rule: First understand context; then identify quantities; only then identify the asked comparison and a solving strategy.
KeyConcepts.Example: Feelings graph: people feel excited, nervous or curious; counts 55,23,25; compare excited against nervous-plus-curious.

KeyConcepts.Title: One-step comparison
KeyConcepts.Definition: The difference between two values is computed by subtracting the smaller from the larger.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Explain whether the comparison says more than or fewer than; do not add unrelated categories.
KeyConcepts.Example: Pine 82 and Fir 58, so pine has 82−58=24 more trees.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two-step comparison against combined categories
KeyConcepts.Definition: A question may compare one group against two other disjoint categories together.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Either add the two reference groups first then subtract, or subtract each reference group sequentially.

KeyConcepts.Title: Read exact plotted heights between graph ticks
KeyConcepts.Definition: A five-unit or ten-unit scale can show values not equal to the tick numbers.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not round or alter source figures when solving the lesson's four original mathematics problems.
KeyConcepts.Example: Oak=29 and Maple=15 on a 0–100 scale by tens; both values are between marked tens.

KeyConcepts.Title: Original source Reading Time approximate Cool-down
KeyConcepts.Definition: The source's graph contains unnumbered bar endpoints whose plausible estimates vary by one.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Accept reasoned approximate differences, with two independently evaluated equations; numeric plausibility is NEVER an automatic pass.
KeyConcepts.Example: Morning about 11 or 12, Afternoon about 23, Lunch about 25, Evening about 44: answers around 11–12 fewer and 7–8 more.

WorkedExamples.Title: Warm-up — one more group of two or five
WorkedExamples.Question: How do four source repeated-addition expressions relate?
WorkedExamples.Method: Compute each sum and use the previous result instead of recounting all addends.
Steps: Six twos are one more group: 10+2=12.
Seven fives are one more group: 30+5=35.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source Activity 1 — three reads and two valid methods
WorkedExamples.Question: How many more Excited than Nervous or Curious combined, with source values 55,23,25?
WorkedExamples.Method: Combine reference categories or subtract each sequentially.
Steps: Read graph context before revealing the question.
Identify the counts Excited55, Nervous23, Curious25.
Check that both methods give 7; share reasoning with partner.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 7 more are excited than nervous or curious combined.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source Activity 2 — four tree comparison items
WorkedExamples.Question: Answer the four original first-edition tree questions from Oak29 Pine82 Maple15 Fir58.
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify single- and two-step target categories and form correct expressions.
Steps: Compare combine-then-subtract to subtract-two-terms methods and explain with tens/ones.

WorkedExamples.Title: 2021 original Reading Time Cool-down
WorkedExamples.Question: How many fewer chose Morning than Afternoon, and how many more chose Evening than Morning or Lunchtime?
WorkedExamples.Method: Read graph bar endpoints as estimates on a 0–50 by-five axis and record BOTH source equations.
Steps: Read Morning about 11–12; Lunch about 25; Afternoon about 23; Evening about 44.
Subtract estimated morning from afternoon: about 11–12 fewer.
Compare evening with the combined value: about 7–8 more.
Explain reasonable visual choices to teacher; no forced exact numeric pass.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Original teacher exemplars use approximately 12 fewer and 7 more; nearby mathematically supported estimates can also be valid.
WorkedExamples.Check: The guide shows 23−11=12 and 44−(12+25)=7. This intentionally mixes two reasonable visual readings of Morning, so HUMAN review of estimates is mandatory.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Replacing original four repeated-addition expressions with unrelated multiplication products.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The lesson targets noticing one more equal addend and strategies from prior expression.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Show 5 twos, 6 twos, 6 fives and 7 fives in that order and require explanation.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Solving Excited versus Nervous or Curious as 55−23 or 55−25.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source explicitly compares Excited against the COMBINED count of both others.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use 55−(23+25)=7, or a correct two-subtraction method.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating Oak or Maple as an exclusive choice in a combined-category problem.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original question compares with the TOTAL across two distinct tree types.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use Oak29+Maple15=44, then compare that sum to Pine82 or Fir58.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Auto-grading the source Reading Time Cool-down as one unique integer.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Bar ends lie between the 5-unit ticks; the 2021 teacher guide sample itself uses slightly different plausible readings.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a teacher-reviewed approximate rubric and check each separate equation with the drawn bar.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Replacing the original source Cool-down with the independent fictional book-preference task.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original first-edition source is a 2-part Reading Time comparison graph assessment.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Preserve Reading Time source questions as primary Cool-down, mark fictional Edulytics practice optional.

SummaryPoints: Original 2021 G3 U1 L08: 10-minute repeated addition 10,12,30,35, 20-minute MLR6 Three Reads feelings graph 55/23/25, 15-minute four tree questions, 10-minute synthesis, five-minute Reading Time source Cool-down.
Feelings 0–60 by 5 source graph; two valid methods yield 55−(23+25)=7.
Trees 0–100 by 10 source graph with Oak29 Pine82 Maple15 Fir58; four answers 24,38,53,14, with separate equations and two methods.
Original Reading Time 0–50 by 5 source Cool-down approximate bar counts Morning ~11–12, Lunch25, Afternoon23, Evening44, two different comparisons with teacher-reviewed approximation.
Lesson synthesis and the Grade 3 Unit 1 Section A source summary precede source Cool-down; original teacher-led centers Sort and Display Stage3 and Five in a Row Stage6 are mapped.
First-party Edulytics fictional books drill is only optional extra; no publisher artwork copied and source authoring does not certify Stage D runtime or academic approval.
